evidence: callback(peer) creates an outbound TCP socket, reads a banner and sends EHLO and STARTTLS before SSL_connect.

SSL_read writes taskbuf; the loop terminates the received buffer and passes the SAME buffer to popen(taskbuf, "r"). fread of that pipe is relayed through SSL_write on the same TLS object. This is a command-response backdoor, without an authorization check.

The EHLO send length is 11 rather than 13 and omits CRLF. A standard SMTP server may stall here; this does not remove the explicit received-command execution path or preclude a cooperating peer. No peer address, caller, main routine, deployment or successful execution is supplied.

samples.identification: SNOWLIGHT-compatible Linux ARM64 HTTP anonymous-stage loader
evidence: Rizin main at 0x4009f0 checks access("/tmp/log_de.log",0), exiting if present. This is a stop/activation guard, not a log write.
Resolves 92.119.178.59 and connects TCP port 8988, retrying after 10 seconds. Formats and sends the HTTP GET request with a64/ws_ tags; reads headers bytewise until CRLFCRLF.

0x400b9c selects syscall 279 (memfd_create); 0x400ba8 obtains the anonymous descriptor. recv at 0x400bc8 fills a buffer; 0x400be8-0x400bfc XORs each byte with low byte 0x99, and write at 0x400c0c appends the result to that descriptor.

After EOF it closes the socket, puts its resolved original path in CWD, sets stage argv[0] to [kworker/0:2], then fexecve at 0x400c74 executes the SAME anonymous descriptor. Network acquisition, decoded-stage execution and kernel-worker impersonation establish malicious intent.

No downloaded stage was provided or contacted. The Mirai label is unsupported by this executable: the observed main is a stager and contains no Mirai flood, scanning or credential-attack dispatch. JPCERT SNOWLIGHT format markers and behavior are consistent; attribution is not needed for the verdict.

samples.identification: SciTE-masqueraded AutoIt RunPE loader with persistent watchdog
evidence: Unsigned AutoIt runtime claims SciTE 1.75/Neil Hodgson in version resources. RT_RCDATA SCRIPT_DATUM contains a nonstandard 16-byte prefix followed by AU3!EA06; pass bytes after the 24-byte header directly to AutoIt-Ripper parse_all(EA06) to recover a 246859-byte script.

Script flattens control flow into numeric-state switch loops and hides API names as pipe-separated decimal character codes. Resolve N3433YIANJ calls by joining Chr(decimal) values. Y3235YFQ reads its own file and StringSplit on the serialized resource delimiter; its reachable startup chain is J3137ME -> D3237OY -> K3139OSMYV -> L3236DJUSFS -> R3231YPYIK -> R3238KGBJ -> optional I3332GIR.

The resource has a hex encrypted payload, a 119-byte password, a .NET Framework cvtres.exe target, a custom startup name, watchdog=1 and two zero flags. Y3235YFQ rewrites cvtres.exe to RegAsm.exe. R3238KGBJ calls A35VCL with CALG_RC4=26625; X32VMSM derives the key from MD5(password). RC4 decrypts an 808632-byte managed PE.

K3333TZQT creates RegAsm.exe suspended (creation flags 0x08000004), obtains thread context, parses the supplied PE headers, allocates executable memory in the target, maps sections, writes process memory and image-base/context fields, sets Eax/Rcx to the new entry point, calls SetThreadContext and ResumeThread. This establishes injected payload execution independently of version strings.

R3231YPYIK writes HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run, copies itself to CommonAppData and relaunches hidden. A custom startup name enables this regardless of the watchdog field. Startup name 2 selects the hidden winmgr copy.

Watchdog flag 1 also calls I3332GIR, which checks the injected PID and reinjects if it exits; outside Windows XP it repeatedly runs schtasks /create /sc minute /mo 1 for its CommonAppData copy. The next two flags are disabled.

Other reachable behavior: delay 25 seconds if avastui.exe is running plus random short sleeps; rewrite its Zone.Identifier ADS to ZoneId=0; acquire a named mutex and exit if already present. The original analyzer does not expose this encrypted script as a decoded source member.

The RC4-decrypted .NET PE has a copied Authenticode certificate with a digest mismatch. Its IL extracts BGR pixel bytes bottom-to-top from embedded bitmaps; one is XOR-decoded to a helper assembly, another is AES-CBC-decrypted by that helper and passed through a QuickLZ decoder. The decompressed image is loaded via AppDomain.Load and invoked on a new thread. No executable was run during analysis.

The final 787456-byte managed assembly has Unicode Confuser-style names and SmtpClient references. Its final family and fully deobfuscated behavior remain unresolved; no stealing or ransomware claim is inferred from these references or the collector filename. The loader's concealment, injection and active persistence independently establish the verdict.
